heading: Real models spread features across many neurons, or hold sparse features SAEs can recover
definition: real models spread features across many neurons, or contain sparse features a dictionary (SAE) can recover.
summary: Many independent groups report features spread across neurons or recovered by sparse autoencoders (SAEs), in protein, vision and audio models and in language models such as Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-9B, with thinner evidence above 10B parameters, such as Gemma-3-27B, and none for models known to exceed 100B. The evidence is indirect and depends on layer, dictionary and metric: randomized models can match trained ones on automated interpretation, and the two studies that challenge the claim find problems only with particular dictionaries.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: R2 (arXiv:2309.08600, Pythia-70M residual SAEs and Pythia-410M IOI patching; studies/superposition.md lists it as an independent test). 1-10B: R2 (e.g. arXiv:2502.16681, Gemma-2-9B). 10-100B: R2 on narrower evidence (named example: the auxiliary feature-overlap analysis in arXiv:2606.00356, Gemma-3-27B). >100B: ? (counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no >100B key; undisclosed sizes fall under its 'not stated' key). Toy: not applicable to V4, and versions.V4.studies_by_size has no toy key.
suggested_status.reason: All counts keys cited in this status, in by_scale, reason and open_questions, come from counts built from the verdict records before the checks, so they still carry pre-check labels and relations. counts: versions.V4.original_sources_linked is empty. studies/superposition.md lists arXiv:2309.08600 (Cunningham et al.; Pythia-70M residual SAEs, Pythia-410M IOI patching) as an independent V4 test, and the checks confirm its supports verdict. counts: versions.V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 2; versions.V4.studies_tested is 131. Other families and scales: arXiv:2502.16681 (reviewed; Gemma-2-9B, Gemma Scope 131k at L0=114, single-latent probes on curated tasks). Only its supports verdict is used here, and the authors treat probing utility as a proxy. arXiv:2606.00356 adds an auxiliary feature-overlap analysis (Gemma-3-27B, Gemma Scope 2 16k JumpReLU SAEs, 300 FLORES+ sentences): semantic pairs have mean Jaccard 0.39 versus 0.13 for random partners. The checks put arXiv:2606.00356 in tranche T5. Its main controlled results qualify semantic readings of individual SAE features across languages and scripts, which bears on V5 rather than V4. counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size includes <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B. The level is for the existential, indirect claim. counts: versions.V4.verdicts also records limits_scope and challenges, but under pre-check labels. The checks moved one V4 challenges verdict to limits_scope and one V4 limits_scope verdict (an L1-SAE condition) to challenges, so the challenges study count is unchanged but one of its two studies is different. Both checked challenges hold only for particular dictionaries, and neither is a failed replication of the existential claim, so R2 stands. The checks also set several V4 limits_scope labels to none or supports, so the limits_scope figures under versions.V4.verdicts will not match the checked labels until counts are rebuilt. In arXiv:2501.17727, randomized and Step-0 Pythia models get similar or higher automated-interpretation scores than trained ones (its limits_scope verdict, which the checks confirm). So automated interpretation alone does not show learned features. The authors keep this metric limit apart from any claim that SAEs fail to recover learned features. Its token-entropy supports verdict is not used, since the checks say it should be none.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would matched ground-truth recovery and neuron-participation tests keep the result across a broad set of semantic features? Would random-model controls like those in arXiv:2501.17727 still match trained models when applied to supervised probing and causal checks, rather than to automated interpretation alone? A main, controlled V4 test at 10-100B, rather than an auxiliary analysis, would firm up that scale. Tests with disclosed >100B sizes and paired preference/RL-stage comparisons would extend coverage (counts: versions.V4.studies_by_stage has no preference/RL key). A failed replication of the existential distribution/recoverability claim with matched, capable methods would move the level toward C. Failures of specific dictionaries or conditions would not (counts: versions.V4.studies_with_challenges is 2, built before the checks; after the checks one of the two challenges studies is a different study).

sources.headline: Pythia sparse autoencoder (SAE) features scored above neuron, PCA and ICA bases on automated interpretability.
A weekday plane found via Mistral 7B SAE clusters causally shifted logit differences.
Summing a few polysemantic Pythia neurons recovered compound-word features almost perfectly.
A sparsity metric based on normalized loss indicated sparse features in BERT, TinyStories and GPT-2 embeddings.
GPT-2 XL causal effects required hundreds of neurons; no single neuron sufficed.
An SAE recovered causally active mod-10 number features in Pythia-1.4B.
Gemma Scope SAEs contained a clear 'starts with S' latent aligned with a linear probe's direction.
SAE features out-scored neurons and random baselines on automated interpretation in Gemma and Llama.
Activation squared norms were almost perfectly linearly predictable from the activations, across 329 SAE settings.
SAE features on medical RoBERTa were far more identifiable than dense label attention.
SAEs on text-embedding-3-small recovered interpretable sparse features in paper abstracts.
GPT-2 small weights held many more nearly orthogonal vectors than dimensions.
GPT-2 SAE features scored higher than GPT-2 neurons on interpretability.
In the protein language model ESM-2, SAE features matched far more Swiss-Prot annotation concepts than neurons.
Only about 10% of sampled Llama-3.1-8B SAE features were uninterpretable.
LLaVA-NeXT SAE features matched explanations better than random baselines on region overlap (IoU) and CLIP score.
Attention-output SAEs in GPT-2 Small yielded mostly interpretable features.
Chess and Othello SAEs recovered board-state features far above random-weight baselines.
Single SAE latents in GPT-4 and GPT-2 predicted curated task labels better than residual channels.
An InceptionV1 SAE recovered interpretable features hidden in polysemantic neurons.
Pythia-70M SAE features were rated more interpretable than neurons and proved causally necessary.
Task-specific and web-text GPT-2 Small SAEs had many high-F1 detectors of indirect object identification (IOI) attributes.
Label-selected SAE latents detected concepts nearly as well as DiffMean and probes.
LLaMA-3-8B concepts were carried by substantial neuron populations; sparse encodings were rare.
Dense SAE latents reflected a real dense model subspace tracking position, part of speech and entropy.
Over pre-training, Pythia-160M crosscoder feature dimensionality dipped, then rose to about 70% of activation dimensions.
SAEs on OpenCLIP ViT-B/32 recovered semantically pure directions that steer labels.
Mistral-7B geographic signal spread across seemingly polysemantic neurons; an SAE found some coherent features.
A MedCLIP SAE found 21 accurate concept detectors versus 2 raw neurons.
GPT-2 small SAEs separated polysemous word senses modestly above chance.
Llama 3.2 1B SAE features beat neurons for language identification.
Single SAE latents in speaker embeddings predicted Spanish speech and hold music.
Vision-encoder SAE latents were far more monosemantic than original neurons at every width.
Entropy estimates gave Pythia-70M's 512-dimensional MLP output 5,600 or 10,000 effective features; the paper states both.
Knowledge in 20 open LLMs was spread across shared, weakly specialized neurons.
Sparse dictionaries reconstructed Gemma2 and Llama3.1 entity activations almost perfectly.
Gemma-2 SAE features beat PCA, ICA, random bases and neurons for factual recall.
Using eight active latents of 4,096, a dictionary reconstructed KV-cache vectors at about 0.81–0.86 cosine similarity.
Qwen2-Audio SAE features beat raw activations on interpretability, steering and monosemanticity.
A Top-k SAE reconstructed e5-large-v2 sentence embeddings with 0.926 explained variance.
SAEs on document embeddings yielded hundreds to thousands of validated interpretable features.
Gemma Scope features captured 75.6% of target bigrams; neurons captured 0%.
Genomic LM SAEs recovered causally validated transcription-factor binding features.
Strongly activating crosscoder latents in three MoE LLMs had well-above-chance explanation F1.
In Gemma-2 9B-it, SAE directions separated tasks where Fisher-important neurons did not.
Gemma-2 SAEs recovered place-cell-like features tiling bracket depth.
Grammatical single-unit selectivity was rare across seven LLMs; whole-vector probes succeeded.
Text-to-MIDI SAEs recovered most next-token loss; one direction controlled program choice.
Whisper SAE latents tracked nameable properties and steered transcripts as expected.
SAE-basis probes beat neuron and PCA bases at predicting MoE router choices.
Claude 3 Sonnet SAE features rarely matched single neurons and were more interpretable.
BiRNA-BERT SAE features were enriched for RNA structure and RNA type.
Histopathology SAE features were more coherent than raw, PCA and random directions.
Geneformer SAEs reconstructed most variance and yielded target-specific, ontology-annotated features.
An IndexTTS2 SAE found emotion-selective features whose steering shifted emotion.
ESM-3 SAE features were mostly enriched for Gene Ontology terms and matched across protein models.
Dense (non-MoE) models needed many FFN neurons per concept, consistent with distributed features.
Chess transformer dictionary features were rated more consistent than MLP neurons.
In deep layers, conjunction computations were spread over 15–40 units; no single unit reproduced one.
Navigation transformers packed thousands of intersection directions into compressed subspaces.
A Pythia-70M SAE feature for LaTeX '$' was sparse, interpretable and spread over neurons.
Sparse-coding features beat neuron and random directions on autointerpretation.
Gelu-1l SAE features were spread across neurons and mostly interpretable.
Pythia-70M SAE features beat baselines on autointerpretation and gave finer IOI edits.
One-layer transformer SAE features were far more interpretable than its MLP neurons.
A small nanoGPT MLP yielded more recurring features than its 128 dimensions.
GPT-2 small SAEs of all sizes recovered weekday, month and year features.
Attention SAEs in GPT-2 Small isolated a few causally relevant IOI features.
ChessGPT and OthelloGPT SAEs recovered board state well above random-init baselines.
OpenAI's GPT-2 small SAE directions matched concepts far better than neurons.
TinyStories SAE features spread across many neurons; one neuron was the largest component of 475 features.
GPT2-small residual SAEs explained 91–99% of variance with few active features.
On GPT2-Small's IOI task, SAE-feature edits approached or beat the accuracy of supervised-feature edits.
A gelu-2l attention-output SAE recovered mostly interpretable, causally active features.
TinyStories SAE features and sparse features from MLP distillation were rated more interpretable than neuron-like units.
A CLIP ViT-L SAE recovered interpretable features where MLP neurons looked polysemantic.
A GPT-2 small layer-0 SAE recovered about 50 positional features tiling all positions.
Sparse SAE-latent probes detected harmful intent near-perfectly in-distribution on Gemma-2 9B.
Claude 3 Sonnet SAEs recovered sparse features poorly matched by any single neuron.
Interpretable genomic LM SAE latents far outnumbered interpretable MLP neurons and detected concepts more accurately.
Consensus SAE on Pythia-70m found a dedicated feature for each of eight token classes.
Lexical entailment in fine-tuned BERT was spread across neurons, not localized to neuron groups.
GPT-2 Small neurons trailed distributed alignment search on factual knowledge; authors infer polysemantic neurons, distributed concepts.
OthelloGPT SAE features predicted tile stability and color, though without a control baseline.
Trained Pythia SAE latents were explained above chance, unlike Gaussian-embedding controls.
Single Gemma Scope SAE latents detected answerability at around 0.8 in-domain.
Individual Gemma-2-9B SAE latents predicted curated task concepts with high test AUC.
SAEs on protein model ESM2-3B matched 233 of 476 Swiss-Prot annotation concepts at F1 above 0.5.
SAE latents on Gemma-2-2B outscored neuron, PCA and residual-channel baselines on automated interpretability.
Selected Llama-3.1-8B SAE latents fired specifically on linguistic features and steered them.
LLaVA-Next SAE features were interpretable, and class steering vectors were sparse in that basis.
Most semi-nonnegative matrix factorization features of MLP activations detected their concepts; single neurons served several features.
A MAIRA-2 SAE yielded 288 interpretable features (1.8%) with F1 above 0.75.
Gemma-2 SAEs reconstructed most variance, and selected features scored F1 above 0.9.
A chemical LM's SAE probes slightly beat neuron probes on 7 of 10 functional groups.
Hand-picked RiNALMo SAE features tracked sequence runs and RNA structural contexts.
SMI-TED SAE features beat neurons on rare motifs and tracked descriptors with far fewer units.
In a molecular transformer, SAE fragment detectors beat random and PCA bases on specificity.
Single SAE latents in antibody language models predicted IGHJ gene identity.
Across SAE architectures, latents captured known probabilistic context-free grammar concepts better than the raw basis.
In GraphCast, one SAE feature detected tropical cyclones while the best neuron was near random.
SAEs on Dream-7B and LLaDA-8B gave good sparsity-fidelity trade-offs and interpretable features.
Attention-output SAE latents classified well above chance on most tasks in three LLMs.
A TopK SAE on a clinical transformer recovered 85-92% of variance with coherent features.
Dictionaries recovered sparse atoms aligned with the state updates that Gated DeltaNet and Mamba-2 layers write.
A GPT-2 small sparse autoencoder (SAE) reconstructed 99.8% of variance; every name tested had selective features.
Gemma-3-27B SAE features were shared across English and Russian paraphrases well above baseline.
Projections onto SAE decoder directions were far more heavy-tailed than random or PCA directions.
SAE features in a text-to-speech model detected concepts and steered laughter, gender and rate.
SAEs on trained GPT-2 kept many features stable across SAE seeds, unlike SAEs on random GPT-2.
Ablating single-token SAE features lowered target-token logits beyond matched controls across models.
Qwen3-Embedding SAE reconstructions preserved retrieval quality, and selected latents had interpretable meanings.
Part-of-speech information in LLaMA-3-8B concentrated in about 500 of 130k SAE latents.
Top SAE features in a protein model matched known disordered-region grammars in four examples.
One SAE feature fired on negation across English, Vietnamese, French and Chinese inputs.
Single SAE latents ranked variable-role positives over matched negatives well above chance in five systems.
SAEs beat PCA at recovering human-labelled concepts in all six text-to-speech models.
An SAE tentatively recovered hundreds of monosemantic features from a tiny LM's MLP layer.
Single SAE task features in Phi-3 Mini and Gemma 1 2B restored task-specific performance.
GPT-2-small SAE codes reconstructed residual activations with reasonable trends on-distribution.
Class-aligned SAE features recurred for some CIFAR-100 classes in LLaVA-Gemma-2B; others aligned partly.
A 64x SAE on CLIP ViT-g-14 embeddings gave a sparse, interpretable code.
SAE features out-scored native coordinates and random rotations on specificity in 103M LMs.
Across seven LLMs, features were sparse combinations of polysemantic neurons, especially in early layers.
SAE directions in Pythia 70M and Llama-2 7B gave coherent token groups, unlike neurons.
Sparse autoencoder (SAE) gains over ICA faded in later layers; MLP dictionaries had many dead units.
Distributed coding varied with layer, feature type and scale; some middle-layer neurons looked monosemantic.
In Pythia-1.4B, features for numbers modulo 10 failed to transfer and sat mostly in single neurons.
No GemmaScope SAE latent matched logistic-regression probe F1; feature recovery varied strongly with active-latent count (L0).
Gemma 2 9b SAE features in the earliest layers scored lower on interpretability.
An LLM could not identify about 42% of active features in DILA's medical-coding SAE dictionary.
GPT-2 SAE features reportedly only matched neurons on OpenAI's interpretability metrics; Anthropic-metric gains shrank with depth.
SAEs on random-weight ESM-2 still recovered hundreds of amino-acid features.
Feature interpretability in a multimodal model varied with concept, judge and layer depth.
Attention-output SAEs were less interpretable in some GPT-2 Small and Gemma-2B layers.
Board-game SAEs reached only about 0.5 single-feature coverage of board properties; chess strategy properties scored low.
GPT-2 small SAE probe scores peaked, then fell as active latents per token neared model width.
GemmaScope SAE latents detected concepts above chance but well below supervised methods like difference-in-means (DiffMean).
Dense SAE latents reflected intrinsically dense residual structure, and under half were explained.
Pythia-6.9B crosscoder features covered proportionally fewer activation dimensions than a smaller Pythia's, attributed to dictionary size.
Only 67 of 32,768 placename SAE features were spatially coherent; most never activated.
Single Llama3-8B SAE latents recovered labelled concepts only moderately above chance.
MedCLIP SAE features were only slightly more monosemantic than raw neurons.
Most TopK and JumpReLU SAE variants scored near chance on polysemous-word precision.
GemmaScope SAEs beat neurons at language identification slightly or not at all; English was nearly unrecoverable.
In most voice-embedding SAE setups, one latent detected Spanish with only about 70% recall.
Vision-language SAE monosemanticity gains shrank with looser sparsity, very wide SAEs and early layers.
Knowledge spreading across parameters shrank with model scale, newer releases and concept frequency.
In Gemma2-2B, recovering sparse features needed enough SAE capacity and depended on the SAE's activation function.
Deep-layer attention value vectors looked dense: SAEs with 8 active latents reached only 0.658–0.728 reconstruction fidelity.
SAE steering from Happy to Angry in an AudioLLM was weaker than on other tasks.
Validated monosemantic topic features declined as more latents were active per document and as dictionaries grew.
Many late-layer transcoder features were single neurons, and bigram recovery depended on training objective.
Dictionaries found few or no features selective for the GATA1 DNA-binding motif in either genomic model.
MoE expert explanations reached only moderate F1 and poorly captured weaker activations.
In Gemma models, fewer features were selective for ordinal quantities, mostly detecting boundary values.
Single Whisper SAE latents detected syntactic, morphological and semantic features only partially.
At gpt-oss-20b layer 16, the SAE basis fell below neuron and PCA probes.
BiRNA-BERT SAE features showed weak enrichment and small effect sizes, especially at layer 0.
Histopathology SAE advantages shrank against strong baselines and varied with the backbone.
scGPT SAE features showed no causal specificity; Geneformer evidence hinged on construction choices.
Only 40.3% of ESM-2 SAE features were enriched for Gene Ontology terms; ESM-3's were more interpretable.
MoE experts with sparse routing concentrated concepts in single neurons rather than spreading them.
Several recovered chess-transformer features had low recall on human tactical and spatial concepts.
Early-layer operators and token-level features sat in single units, not spread across many.
SAEs on a 31M-parameter transformer gave no clear evidence of recovering real sparse features.
Features poorly matched across dictionaries (low MCS) were mostly dead or looked more polysemantic.
Sparse-coding features beat baselines only under some auto-interpretation scoring choices.
About 60% of gelu-1l SAE latents formed an ultra-low-frequency, uninterpretable cluster.
Pythia-70M SAEs showed no clear interpretability gain in final layers and imperfect reconstruction.
Fewer SAE directions matched concepts in later layers, with no edge over neurons at layers 8–9.
TinyStories SAE reconstruction raised loss about 25%, recovering the MLP's computation only partly.
GPT-2 Small residual SAEs degraded downstream loss more in later layers and long contexts.
Recovery of indirect-object-identification features depended on SAE architecture and selection; vanilla SAEs lagged in edit accuracy.
About half of the ViT SAE features aligned with a few MLP neurons.
Gemma Scope SAE latents recovered first-letter features unreliably, far below linear probes.
SAE-latent probes transferred worse out of distribution than dense probes.
No genomic-model SAE latent passed the F1 threshold at the first MLP layer.
Distributed alignment in BERT on MoNLI was less complete at layer 7 than 9.
OpenAI's GPT-2 Small SAE mediated country and continent only as well as neurons.
SAE reconstructions carried task features less fully than supervised dictionaries; SAE edits on indirect-object identification failed.
Randomized and step-0 Pythia models matched or beat trained ones on SAE auto-interp scores.
Top SAE features detecting answerable questions reached only about 70% on Gemma-2-2B; preliminary Llama testing failed.
For some probing tasks, the best single SAE latent fit poorly or tracked spurious cues.
SAEs on small ESM2-8M recovered only 15.1–20.0% of concepts; the 3B model did better.
SAEs on a randomly initialised Pythia-1B scored only slightly lower on auto-interp.
Single-latent interventions on linguistic features had weak effects, only modestly above random controls.
LlaVA-Next neurons were highly interpretable; SAE features were only slightly better.
Concept-detection scores fell sharply in late Llama layers and degraded in Gemma as feature count rose.
Nearly half of radiology-model SAE features scored below random under automated interpretation.
Chemical-model SAE features showed only modest property associations and no edge for some groups.
Some RNA-model SAE features lacked dominant structure, and layer 1 activations were diffuse.
For common chemical motifs, single neurons performed nearly as well as SAE features.
Molecular-transformer SAE features fell below random/PCA baselines on amide, modestly above on urea.
Antibody-model SAEs found no qualifying features for some genes, such as IGHJ5.
Single SAE latents recovered known concepts far from ideally; probes did significantly better.
GraphCast SAEs found no blocking-event feature; the atmospheric-river advantage over neurons was small.
Diffusion-LM SAEs needed more active latents (L0) in deep layers; some features scored low on auto-interpretation.
GPT2-Small SAE accuracy was near or modestly above chance on most tasks; Emotions was weak everywhere.
Clinical-model SAE features were only category-level coherent; explained variance depended strongly on K, the active-latent count.
Replacing recurrent-state updates with SAE dictionary atoms performed at chance in Qwen3.5-4B, DeltaNet and RWKV-7.
Text-to-speech SAE features scored modestly on audio labels; no layer-0 coordinate separated concepts.
Gemma-3-1B single-token SAE features were causally necessary in only some layers.
Raw activations beat SAE latents at part-of-speech prediction; the latents had low precision on controlled text.
An SAE feature chosen to detect negation barely fired on negated Vietnamese inputs in Llama-3.1-8B.
SAE features chosen for code-variable roles fell to chance on role-changing edits, tracking broad concepts instead.
In voice-cloning TTS models, SAEs rarely isolated concepts; PCA and random directions beat them overall.
On LLaVA image tokens, a text-trained SAE's top early-layer features were unrelated to the image.
An SAE on CLIP image embeddings explained only 65% of their variance on diverse LAION-2B images.
L1 SAEs scored below a random basis on interpretability in both dense and expert-based MoWE models.
Higher-level contextual features like is_python_code appeared to sit in single dedicated neurons, not spread across many.
SAE feature recovery worsened in later Pythia-70M layers and when too few features fired per input.
Public SAEs on Pythia-70M and Gemma2-2B did no better than chance at separating word senses.
Bloom's and Apollo's SAEs separated country from continent knowledge worse than neurons did in GPT-2 Small.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: V4 tests in models with explicitly disclosed parameter size above 100B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no >100B key. GPT-4 and Claude 3 Sonnet records leave parameter size undisclosed; these cannot establish that size coverage.

untested.what: Matched tests isolating the effects of preference/RL training on feature distribution and dictionary recoverability, including trajectories through pretraining and instruction tuning.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_stage has base, instruct/chat and fine-tuned categories but no preference/RL key. Pretraining snapshots, base/instruct examples and transferred base-model SAEs do not supply the matched stage trajectory.

untested.what: A systematic joint neuron-by-feature map and ground-truth dictionary-recovery evaluation across a broad semantic feature set in a general-purpose LLM.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines distinguish neuron distribution tests without SAE recovery from rule-defined concept recovery without neuron-spread measurements. Small-model decoder-density and selected-feature participation tests do exist, so neuron participation itself is not wholly untested. counts: versions.V4.main_rows_by_operation and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation describe separate measurement, probing and intervention coverage, without establishing this joint evaluation.

wording_issues.issue: Distribution is conditional on feature, layer and architecture. Compound-word features can use a few neurons; successor features can align with individual neurons; late transcoders recover single-neuron features; MoE expert concepts can be recoverable with one neuron.

The evidence mixes MLP neurons, residual-stream coordinates, rotated CLS representations and external embedding dimensions. Weak maximum single-neuron correlation also does not directly count neuron participation. In Qwen3-0.6B last-token residual coordinates, 3 of 68 paradigms have one NSI>2 coordinate each (500 permutations). In random good–good and bad–bad controls, 0 of 68 do (200 permutations). That rarity of single-coordinate selectivity does not by itself show features spread across coordinates.

Few active dictionary features per token and sparse support in the neuron basis are different properties. 'Sparse' can also be judged against the hidden dimension or against the dictionary size. In gelu-1l (16384-feature SAE), about 92.1% of the non-ultra-low-frequency decoder vectors are dense across neurons, while dictionary activations are sparse. Dense-subspace ablation shows that some SAE-recovered structure is intrinsically dense. That dense structure sits alongside recoverable sparse features and does not test whether they are absent. Imposed TopK activity alone does not establish semantic recovery.

Recovery needs a stated criterion: reconstruction, concept detection, natural-language interpretation and causal control can disagree. Two results limit particular dictionaries: chance word-meaning separation in open Pythia-70M and Gemma2-2B SAEs, and factual disentanglement below neurons for Bloom and Apollo GPT-2-small SAEs (the Open AI SAE matches neurons). In SAGE, even 16 sparse edits on GPT-2-small IOI subject/order groups fail to significantly influence predictions. That measures sparse control, not whether features are recovered. Results can reverse within one condition. At matched post-block sites in dense 103.5M and MoWE 274.2M LMs, L1 SAEs score below their own random bases on automated-judge interpretability (0.332 vs 0.417; 0.393 vs 0.455), while TopK SAEs at the same sites score above them. These results show neither recovery by every dictionary nor failure of every possible dictionary.

Some supporting records use SNMF, crosscoders, transcoders or Lorsa rather than ordinary SAEs, and their objectives and target representations differ. For example, SNMF (k=100–400) on MLP activations of Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-2B and GPT-2 Small yields sparse linear combinations of neurons, so that study's support does not rest on ordinary SAE feature recovery.

The packs include vision encoders, weather GNNs, specialist biological or clinical models and synthetic-navigation transformers. These give analogous representation findings whose scope is narrower than, or different from, natural-language LLM evidence. For two of them the checks find no V4 verdict warranted, because V4 names LLMs: the coded-clinical-sequence transformer (FlatASCEND) and the GPT-2-style transformers trained on synthetic Manhattan navigation. Their rows are cannot_determine for V4 as written. Counting such systems as V4 evidence would mean broadening V4 explicitly.

Distributed causal effects and interpretable dictionaries do not by themselves establish capacity-driven superposition. Automated interpretation can also favor random-model features, and recurrent atom reconstruction does not separate superposition from structure the reconstruction itself creates. The random-model controls limit what auto-interpretation scores say about learned representations. They do not show failed sparse-feature recovery in trained models, where explainable sparse Pythia SAE latents remain observed V4 evidence.

The existential wording fits selected recoverable features. It does not imply that such features are common across the dictionary, that reconstruction is complete, or that the features are canonical model units. The negation evidence rests on one selected feature per model, read off token firing counts on 150 negative and 150 affirmative synthetic extraction examples per language, and how common such features are in the dictionary is untested. The selected Gemma-3-4B feature also fires on some affirmative-example tokens (negative/affirmative: tôi 29/29, Tôi 15/15, 很 3/41, against not 132/0). Inserting an SAE into a language model can raise downstream loss. Interpretable examples sit alongside uninterpretable or dead regions. About 60% of gelu-1l latents are ultra-low-frequency and anecdotally uninterpretable, though no truly dead features are reported. Most inspected low-MCS Pythia-70M features were dead.

method_sensitivity.what: BERT-base (MoNLI-fine-tuned, CLS) lexical-entailment DAS IIA is 0.88–0.91 at layer 7 versus 1.00 at layer 9, against localist 0.47 and brute-force 0.64 baselines (Table 2). Pythia residual interpretation advantages weaken late, while attention-feature interpretation varies by layer. Gemma-3-1B single-token feature ablation significantly lowers target logits in 9/26 GemmaScope layers versus 18/25 BatchTopK layers. So layerwise necessity varies with layer and SAE family, while recovered single-token features are present under both. Layer effects need not have the same direction across models or metrics.

method_sensitivity.factor: Dictionary architecture, objective, width and active-feature budget
method_sensitivity.what: PS-Eval differs across ReLU, TopK and JumpReLU-STE settings. TSAE recovery requires capacity appropriate to data scale. Qwen3-4B bigram matching differs between Matryoshka and plain TopK objectives. At the same post-block sites of the dense and MoWE language models, TopK SAEs exceed their random-basis controls on automated-judge interpretability, while L1 SAEs fall below theirs: dense 0.332 versus 0.417, and MoWE 0.393 versus 0.455.

For Pythia-70M's selected LaTeX-$ feature, a fixed activation threshold of 0.5 gives 3 neurons, whereas neuron-specific thresholds give 60. The weight-based estimate is broader still. NanoGPT's effective-neuron counts are similar to random vectors, so broad decoder support alone does not distinguish learned semantic organization.

AxBench (CONCEPT500): GemmaScope latents matched to concepts by their auto-interpretation label score AUROC 0.735 at Gemma-2-2B L10 and 0.631 at L20, versus same-site DiffMean 0.948 and 0.955. Latents chosen by AUROC on the labelled training set (SAE-A) score 0.907–0.924 held-out across the four sites (verdict text, no row). Interpretation-aware IOI selection loses edit accuracy. MoE explanations score better in the strongest activation bin than overall.

method_sensitivity.factor: Interpretation metric, scoring set and judge
method_sensitivity.what: Pythia70M's combined top-and-random residual score shows no neuron-basis advantage, whereas separate-set scoring favors learned features; removing MLP feature bias particularly harms random-only scoring. GPT2-SAE gains differ between Anthropic and OpenAI metrics. LLaVA-NeXT-LLaMA3-8B SAE explanations score part consistency 0.90 and colour consistency 0.92 with a GPT-4o judge (100 cases; called GPT-4 in Section 3.2), versus 0.60 for both from human raters (60 samples and 120 evaluations overall; per-category counts not stated). In voice-cloning TTS, SAE top-2 human-concept nF1 exceeds PCA in all six models. On extractor-derived concepts, SAE leads its within-model baselines (PCA, random directions, untrained SAE) only in Qwen3-TTS. Two-feature recovery is limited relative to all-feature recovery across feature sets.

method_sensitivity.factor: Random-model controls and the property being measured
method_sensitivity.what: Randomized Pythia models can match or exceed trained models' automated-interpretation scores. SAEBench's random-initialized Pythia-1B keeps relatively high auto-interpretability despite weak supervised performance (Appendix E, verdict text, no row). Randomized-weight ESM-2-8M SAEs give no biological Swiss-Prot-concept features but hundreds of amino-acid-type-associated features. GPT-2 cross-seed feature stability distinguishes trained from random models under the reported matching-threshold sweeps. Whether random models resemble trained ones depends on the property scored. These controls test what each metric measures; they do not test recovery in trained models.

method_sensitivity.factor: Host architecture, routing, scale and concept prevalence
method_sensitivity.what: MoE experts permit more single-neuron concept recovery than dense comparators, with dependence on routing sparsity and expert selection. WriteSAE substitution and register recovery vary across recurrent hosts and scales. ESM2 concept recovery changes with model size. Knowledge specialization (PSS) increases with model size in Qwen1.5 0.5B–14B and is higher for more popular concepts, while knowledge sharing across MLP vectors remains evident.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training distribution, language, transfer and context length
method_sensitivity.what: Chat-data SAE training (from scratch or finetuned) improves Gemma-2-9B-IT harmful-intent probing over the original GemmaScope SAEs, with no systematic advantage among chat-training variants; dense probes stay better. Mostly-English Gemma Scope dictionaries identify languages unevenly: Gemma-2-9B SAE macro F1 is 0.897 versus neuron 0.905 over 15 languages, with English F1 0.000 (0.177 in Gemma-2-2B, verdict reason). An English-selected L13 negation feature from a base-model Llama Scope SAE, applied to an instruct model, fires weakly on Vietnamese negated inputs (thích 3/0 negative/affirmative token firings) but more clearly in French (pas 69/0) and Chinese (喜欢 18/0). A GPT-2-small layer-0 SAE (context_size=128) is stable within its training context. Beyond that context, positional features mislocalize and semantic features become noisier or fire spuriously (text, no row).

CONCH raw-direction retrieval coherence rises from approximately 0.42 under signed-union retrieval to 0.749 with best-tail selection, and random directions reach 0.748, while SAE features stay at 0.835. In the 25M molecular transformer at layer 3, amide SAE specificity is 0.22, versus 0.00 for dense and 0.49 for random/PCA bases, so whether the SAE ranks above or below depends on the comparator. Gemma task separability compares differently selected SAE and neuron directions.

Freezing RMSNorm scaling diminishes the entropy effect of a Gemma-2-2B nullspace-latent ablation. In LinguaLens (Llama-3.1-8B OpenSAE latents, GPT-4o judge), single-latent enhancement and ablation success differ by linguistic feature. Simile ablation succeeds in 48.0% of cases versus 52.0% for a random control (FIC 6.9). These numbers measure how well the interventions work, not whether features are recovered. MIDI program-choice steering is confirmed on disjoint prompts with random-direction comparisons.
